commands.name: adr
commands.title: Architecture Decision Records
commands.description: Create, update, or review an Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
commands.default_action: creating or reviewing an Architecture Decision Record
instructions:
Enforce the 5 Core Tenets:
   - **Intent over Mechanism:** Domain capability and architectural invariants over tool brand names.
   - **Reification over Tribal Memory:** Mechanically enforceable via explicit types, module boundaries, automated CI fitness functions (e.g., ArchUnit, import linter rules), contract tests, or alarms.
   - **Honest Trade-offs & Real Alternatives:** Zero free lunches; evaluate genuine runners-up and state why they were rejected.
   - **Advice Process over Gatekeepers:** Autonomous team ownership with transparent alignment (`Consulted` and `Informed`).
   - **Reversibility & Immutability:** Two-way doors with explicit revisit criteria; immutable accepted history.
Structure the record using the 8-row Tabular Y-Statement, prioritized Decision Drivers (`DRV-01`, `DRV-02`, etc.), and the Multi-Criteria Comparison Matrix.
Pass the Uninformed Reader Test (understandable in 3 minutes) and guard against the 6 Anti-Patterns.
Fulfill the user's specific request: drafting a new ADR or reviewing an existing one.

commands.name: review
commands.title: Bart Adversarial Code Reviewer
commands.description: Critically review code, diffs, or pull requests for bugs, edge cases, and design flaws
commands.default_action: critically reviewing code or a pull request
instructions: Perform an adversarial code review looking for bugs, edge cases, correctness failures, lazy shortcuts, and pattern violations.
Check whether the target repository defines its own review agent via find-repo-agents.sh.
Scrutinize tests, verify real failure modes, and evaluate CI results before providing a clear quality assessment and merge decision.

commands.name: humanize
commands.title: AI Text Humanizer
commands.description: Review and remove signs of AI-generated writing from text, ADRs, or docs
instructions: Scan for AI-isms, inflated vocabulary, formulaic structure, and promotional filler documented in references/patterns.md.
Rewrite problematic sections with natural, direct language while preserving core meaning and voice.
Conduct a final anti-AI critique pass to ensure the text sounds authentically human.

commands.name: c4
commands.title: C4 Architecture Diagrams
commands.description: Generate software architecture documentation using C4 model Mermaid diagrams
instructions: Determine the appropriate C4 abstraction level (C4Context, C4Container, C4Component, C4Deployment) based on the audience.
Analyze the codebase structure and dependencies to accurately map containers, components, and relationships.
Generate valid Mermaid C4 diagrams with explanatory architectural notes.

commands.name: commit
commands.title: Atomic Commit Protocol
commands.description: Structure and format git commits following the Atomic Commit Protocol (ACP)
commands.default_action: formatting and staging an atomic commit
instructions: Enforce the Atomic Commit Protocol (ACP): every commit must be a self-contained, tested, indivisible unit of work.
Verify that implementation and tests are together, tests pass, and code quality checks are satisfied.
Format commit messages strictly adhering to Conventional Commits format (`type(scope): subject`).

commands.name: standup
commands.title: Daily Standup Planner
commands.description: Turn meeting transcripts into actionable daily plans, decisions, and issue updates
instructions: Extract key updates, blockers, decisions, and action items from the meeting transcript or discussion.
Correlate updates with open GitHub issues, project items, or tracking boards.
Generate a clear, sequenced execution plan for the day with assigned ownership.

commands.name: status
commands.title: Daily Status Reporter
commands.description: Generate a factual summary of recent git commits, PRs, and assigned issues
instructions: Gather activity strictly from git logs, GitHub PRs/issues, and project tracking systems.
Prioritize factual recall over speculation: every line must correspond to verified system output.
Format the report into a dated summary suitable for logging to ~/projects/dailies/.

commands.name: bdd
commands.title: Adzic BDD Specification
commands.description: Apply Gojko Adzic Specification by Example principles to feature files and user stories
commands.default_action: refining BDD specifications and feature files
instructions: Apply Gojko Adzic's Specification by Example principles to Gherkin feature files.
Evaluate and optimize scenarios using the Adzic Index.
Ensure business-readable acceptance criteria focused on behavior rather than UI interactions.

commands.name: debug
commands.title: Systematic Debugging
commands.description: Investigate and resolve bugs systematically with root cause analysis before proposing fixes
instructions: Enforce the Iron Law: NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST.

Follow the 4 Systematic Phases: (1) Root Cause Investigation & reproduction, (2) Pattern Analysis & reference comparison, (3) Single-variable Hypothesis testing, (4) Implementation via TDD regression test.

Apply systematic troubleshooting playbooks: backward data-flow tracing (`root-cause-tracing.md`), test pollution isolation (`find-polluter.sh`), condition-based waiting (`condition-based-waiting.md`), and defense-in-depth boundary validation (`defense-in-depth.md`).
Adhere to the 3-strike rule: if 3 fix attempts fail, stop immediately and question the architecture.

commands.name: test-review
commands.title: Test Design Review
commands.description: Critique tests or diffs against Dave Farley's Properties of Good Tests and Gojko Adzic's BDD principles
commands.default_action: reviewing test design and executable specifications
instructions: Evaluate tests against Dave Farley's 6 Properties of Good Tests: Fast, Maintainable, Repeatable, Atomic, Necessary, and Understandable.
Evaluate tests against Gojko Adzic's Specification by Example: Behavior over Implementation, high signal-to-noise ratio (Adzic Index), concrete domain examples, and living documentation.
Produce a structured review report containing the Farley Scorecard, Adzic Scorecard, and line-by-line violation findings with concrete fixes.

commands.name: doctor
commands.title: Branch & PR Doctor
commands.description: Audit branch health, working tree cleanliness, conventional commits, local tests, GitHub CI, and PR well-formedness
commands.default_action: running a comprehensive branch and PR health check
instructions: Run the automated diagnostic check: `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/branch-doctor/scripts/doctor.py`.

Inspect the 5 health dimensions: (1) Working tree cleanliness, (2) Git commit history sanity against Conventional Commits & ACP, (3) Local test suite execution, (4) GitHub Actions CI status, (5) PR existence and well-formedness against PR templates and issue references.
Provide actionable recommendations for any failing or warning health checks.

commands.name: forensics
commands.title: Git Forensics & Code Archaeology
commands.description: Diagnose codebase health, detect bug hotspots, churn, bus factor, and perform git pickaxe archaeology
commands.default_action: analyzing codebase health and git forensics
instructions: Analyze codebase health using `uv run scripts/forensics.py`: churn (codebase drag), bus factor (knowledge silos), bug hotspots, velocity, and rollback commits.
Perform code archaeology using git pickaxe (`uv run scripts/forensics.py pickaxe '<pattern>'`) to find deleted or modified functions across all branches.
Use X-Ray Blame (`uv run scripts/forensics.py xblame <file>`) to ignore whitespace and detect code movement.

commands.name: codemap
commands.title: Codemap Architecture Explorer
commands.description: Map codebase architecture, dependency flow, hub files, and blast radius
instructions: Analyze project structure using `codemap .` and dependency flow via `codemap --deps .`.
Identify architectural hub files and calculate blast radius using `codemap --importers <file>` before modifying shared code.
Generate or inspect cross-agent handoff context envelopes via `codemap handoff .`.

commands.name: trace
commands.title: Macro-to-Micro Codebase Tracing
commands.description: Trace bugs and refactoring blast radius by chaining Codemap, LSP, and AST-grep
commands.default_action: tracing structural code dependencies and blast radius
instructions: Follow the 3-tier articulation chain: Macro (Codemap file graph) -> Meso (LSP symbol graph) -> Micro (AST-grep syntax tree).
Identify hub files and dependency blast radius with Codemap before editing.
Trace call chains and data flow with LSP (`lsp reference`, `lsp definition`, `lsp outline`).
Perform surgical syntax-aware transformations using AST-grep (`sg run`).

commands.name: lessons
commands.title: Lessons Learned Retrospective
commands.description: Extract software engineering principles, takeaways, and anti-patterns from recent commits or diffs
commands.default_action: extracting software engineering lessons from recent work
instructions: Determine analysis scope: feature branch (`git log main..HEAD` + `git diff main...HEAD`), last N commits, or specific SHA.
Load core software engineering principles catalog from `references/se-principles.md` and `references/anti-patterns.md`.
Extract actionable, grounded software engineering lessons demonstrating what the code changes prove or caution against.

commands.name: todo
commands.title: Todo Navigator
commands.description: Navigate project tasks, inspect roadmap, and view or edit task cards in shadow cache
commands.default_action: navigating project tasks and inspecting the roadmap
instructions: Inspect the project roadmap using `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py status`.
To view a specific task card, run `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py view <id>`.

To edit a task card interactively, execute `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py edit <id>`. If tmux is active, this automatically opens an interactive vim popup and blocks until the user exits vim.

IMPORTANT: If Antigravity sends this command to the background while the user edits in the popup, DO NOT poll or monitor it (no manage_task, no ps aux, no reading task logs). Simply inform the user the popup is open and STOP calling tools. The system will automatically wake you when the user finishes editing.
Support express operations (`done`, `P0-P3`, `add <text>`) via `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py edit <id> <ops>`.
Keep chat responses concise: never dump the full 30+ line markdown card into chat on an edit command.

commands.name: next
commands.title: Next Task Selector
commands.description: Select the next unblocked, highest-leverage task and page in its acceptance criteria card
instructions: Run `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py next` to pull the highest-WSJF unblocked task.
Page in the task card content directly into context and present actionable next steps to the user.
Provide a clickable file:// link to the task card for direct editing.

commands.name: prev
commands.title: Previous Work Recall
commands.description: Recall what was just worked on: 3-line factual summary of last completed task and git commit
commands.default_action: recalling the last completed work and git commit
instructions: Run `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py prev`.
Output the concise 3-line factual summary strictly based on the system output.
Do not speculate or propose new actions unless explicitly asked.

commands.name: replan
commands.title: Todo Replanner & Bootstrapper
commands.description: Bootstrap task backlog or replan outstanding tasks with topological DAG sorting and WSJF waves
commands.default_action: bootstrapping or replanning the project task backlog
instructions: Run `uv run {SKILLS_DIR}/todo-navigator/scripts/todo_engine.py replan`.
If the backlog is empty, bootstrap initial tasks and goal from git context and specifications.
Highlight critical path bottlenecks (tasks blocking downstream items) and execution waves.
